newsitem.title: USA: Sears says uncollectibles provision rises.
newsitem.headline: Sears says uncollectibles provision rises.

text.p: Sears Roebuck and Co said Thursday that its domestic provision for uncollectible accounts increased 18.9 percent to $269 million in the first quarter from $227 million in the year-ago period.

"The increase in account charge-offs reflects the continuation of an industry-wide increase in personal bankruptcies and delinquencies, as well as growth in the credit receivable portfolio," Sears said.

Excluding the impact of a related accounting change, Sears said the provision for uncollectible accounts would have grown by $124 million, or 54.9 percent, "largely due to a 56.4 percent increase in account charge-offs experienced in the first quarter."

The accounting change on credit card securitization increased 1997 first quarter net income by $38 million. The retailing giant reported first quarter net income of $182 million on sales of $8.76 billion, compared to year-ago earnings of $151 million on sales of $7.99 billion.
Sears said its domestic credit portfolio, which consists primarily of Sears Card customer receivables, continued to perform well in the first quarter.
"Credit revenues increased by 12.3 percent due to higher receivable balances, which were driven by strong merchandise sales and the impact of uniform pricings," Sears said.
The retailer's net interest margin on the first quarter, on a pre-accounting change basis, improved by $173 million, Sears said.
